```{r development, include=FALSE}
library(testthat)
```

Repeated, optionally stratified k-fold cross-validation, implemented with base R and `data.table`. `split_cv()` works on a list of tables, `nest_cv()` on a nested table such as the output of `w2l_nest()`. Folds are returned as row indices and, optionally, as training / validation subsets (`data.table` or `data.frame`).

# Cross-validation for a list of tables: `split_cv()`
    
```{r function-split_cv}
#' Apply V-Fold Cross-Validation to a List of Datasets
#'
#' @description
#' `split_cv` creates (optionally repeated and stratified) v-fold
#' cross-validation splits for every dataset in a list. It is implemented
#' with base R and `data.table` only and returns, per dataset, a
#' `data.table` of fold identifiers, row indices and (optionally) the
#' training / validation subsets.
#'
#' @param data     A `list` whose every element is a `data.frame` or
#'   `data.table`. Must be non-empty. A single `data.frame` is not accepted
#'   (wrap it in `list()`).
#' @param v        Number of folds. A single integer >= 2. Default `10`.
#' @param repeats  Number of repeats. A single integer >= 1. Default `1`.
#' @param strata   `NULL` (default) or a single column name present in
#'   **every** dataset. Rows are shuffled within each stratum so that every
#'   fold receives a proportional share of each stratum.
#' @param breaks   Number of quantile bins used when `strata` is numeric with
#'   more than `breaks` distinct values. Default `4`.
#' @param pool     Strata holding less than this proportion of the rows are
#'   merged with the next-smallest stratum. A number in `[0, 0.5)`.
#'   Default `0.1`.
#' @param seed     `NULL` (default) or a single number for reproducible folds.
#'   The caller's random-number stream is restored on exit.
#' @param materialize Logical. If `TRUE` (default), `train` / `validate`
#'   list-columns holding the subsets are added. `FALSE` keeps only the row
#'   indices, which needs far less memory for large data.
#' @param out_type Class of the `train` / `validate` subsets: `"dt"`
#'   (`data.table`, default) or `"df"` (plain `data.frame`, e.g. for
#'   'ASReml-R' or other modelling functions that expect a `data.frame`).
#'   Factor levels are kept in full in every subset. Only used when
#'   `materialize = TRUE`; the returned fold table itself is always a
#'   `data.table`.
#'
#' @details
#' Fold sizes differ by at most one row. With stratification, rows are
#' shuffled within strata, the strata are laid out one after another and fold
#' labels are dealt out cyclically, so each stratum is spread evenly across
#' folds. The stratification rules (`breaks`, `pool`) follow the same idea
#' as `rsample::vfold_cv()`, but the random fold assignments are not
#' identical to rsample's.
#'
#' Training and validation subsets can always be rebuilt from the indices:
#' `data[[1]][res[[1]]$train_idx[[k]], ]`.
#'
#' For mixed-model cross-validation (e.g. genomic prediction with
#' 'ASReml-R') a common alternative to subsetting is masking: keep all
#' records, set the phenotypes of `validate_idx` to `NA`, fit the model on
#' the full data and correlate the predicted breeding values of the masked
#' individuals with their observations. `materialize = FALSE` is enough for
#' this, since only the indices are needed.
#'
#' @return A `list` of `data.table` objects (one per input dataset, names of
#'   `data` preserved), each with one row per fold and the columns:
#' \itemize{
#'   \item `id`           — fold label (`Fold1`, ...), or repeat label
#'         (`Repeat1`, ...) when `repeats > 1`.
#'   \item `id2`          — fold label, only when `repeats > 1`.
#'   \item `train_idx`    — list-column of training row indices.
#'   \item `validate_idx` — list-column of validation row indices.
#'   \item `train`, `validate` — list-columns of subsets, `data.table` or
#'         `data.frame` according to `out_type` (only when
#'         `materialize = TRUE`).
#' }
#'
#' @seealso [nest_cv()] for the nested `data.table` variant.
#'
#' @import data.table
#' @export
split_cv <- function(data,
                     v           = 10L,
                     repeats     = 1L,
                     strata      = NULL,
                     breaks      = 4L,
                     pool        = 0.1,
                     seed        = NULL,
                     materialize = TRUE,
                     out_type    = "dt") {

  # -- 1. Input validation (once, before the loop) -----------------------------
  # A data.frame is also a list, so it must be rejected explicitly; otherwise
  # its columns would be treated as datasets.
  if (!is.list(data) || is.data.frame(data))
    stop("`data` must be a list of data.frames/data.tables. ",
         "To use a single data.frame, wrap it in list(). Received: ",
         paste(class(data), collapse = "/"), call. = FALSE)
  if (length(data) == 0L)
    stop("`data` must not be empty.", call. = FALSE)
  v       <- .check_count(v, "v", 2L)
  repeats <- .check_count(repeats, "repeats", 1L)
  breaks  <- .check_count(breaks, "breaks", 2L)
  if (!is.numeric(pool) || length(pool) != 1L || is.na(pool) || pool < 0 || pool >= 0.5)
    stop("`pool` must be a single number in [0, 0.5).", call. = FALSE)
  .check_flag(materialize, "materialize")
  .check_choice(out_type, c("dt", "df"), "out_type")

  is_valid <- vapply(data, is.data.frame, logical(1L))
  if (!all(is_valid)) {
    bad_idx <- which(!is_valid)
    stop("All elements of `data` must be data.frames or data.tables.\n",
         "  Invalid element(s) at index: ", paste(bad_idx, collapse = ", "),
         "\n  Types received: ",
         paste(vapply(data[bad_idx], function(x) class(x)[1L], character(1L)),
               collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  }

  too_small <- vapply(data, nrow, integer(1L)) < v
  if (any(too_small))
    stop("Dataset(s) at index ", paste(which(too_small), collapse = ", "),
         " have fewer rows than `v` (", v, ").", call. = FALSE)

  if (!is.null(strata)) {
    if (!is.character(strata) || length(strata) != 1L || is.na(strata))
      stop("`strata` must be a single character string (column name).", call. = FALSE)
    strata_missing <- vapply(data, function(df) !strata %in% names(df), logical(1L))
    if (any(strata_missing)) {
      missing_idx <- which(strata_missing)
      stop("The `strata` column '", strata,
           "' is absent from dataset(s) at index: ",
           paste(missing_idx, collapse = ", "),
           if (!is.null(names(data)))
             paste0(" (name(s): '", paste(names(data)[missing_idx],
                                          collapse = "', '"), "')"),
           call. = FALSE)
    }
  }

  # -- 2. Fold assignment for every dataset -------------------------------------
  run <- function() {
    out <- lapply(data, function(x) {
      x <- if (data.table::is.data.table(x)) x else data.table::as.data.table(x)
      .vfold_table(x, v = v, repeats = repeats, strata = strata,
                   breaks = breaks, pool = pool, materialize = materialize,
                   out_type = out_type)
    })
    names(out) <- names(data)
    out
  }
  # A non-NULL seed makes the folds reproducible without disturbing the
  # caller's RNG stream.
  .with_seed(seed, run())
}
```
  
```{r example-split_cv}
# Prepare example data: Convert first 3 columns of iris dataset to long format and split
dt_split <- w2l_split(data = iris, cols = 1:3)
# dt_split is now a list containing 3 data tables for Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width, and Petal.Length

# Example 1: Single cross-validation (no repeats)
split_cv(
  data = dt_split,      # Input list of split data
  v = 3,                # Set 3-fold cross-validation
  repeats = 1,          # Perform cross-validation once (no repeats)
  seed = 123            # Reproducible folds
)
# Returns a list where each element contains:
# - id: fold labels (Fold1, Fold2, Fold3)
# - train_idx / validate_idx: row indices of each fold
# - train / validate: training and validation subsets

# Example 2: Repeated cross-validation
split_cv(
  data = dt_split,      # Input list of split data
  v = 3,                # Set 3-fold cross-validation
  repeats = 2,          # Perform cross-validation twice
  seed = 123
)
# Returns a list where each element contains:
# - id: repeat labels (Repeat1, Repeat2)
# - id2: fold labels (Fold1, Fold2, Fold3)
# - train_idx / validate_idx, train / validate

# Example 3: Stratified CV, indices only (memory friendly)
res <- split_cv(dt_split, v = 5, strata = "Species", seed = 1,
                materialize = FALSE)
# Rebuild the training set of fold 1 of the first dataset when needed
head(dt_split[[1]][res[[1]]$train_idx[[1]], ])
```

```{r tests-split_cv}
test_that("split_cv creates complete, disjoint and balanced folds", {
  res <- split_cv(list(a = iris), v = 4, seed = 1)$a
  expect_identical(res$id, paste0("Fold", 1:4))
  v_idx <- res$validate_idx
  expect_identical(sort(unlist(v_idx)), 1:150)
  expect_true(max(lengths(v_idx)) - min(lengths(v_idx)) <= 1)
  for (k in 1:4) {
    expect_length(intersect(res$train_idx[[k]], v_idx[[k]]), 0)
    expect_identical(nrow(res$validate[[k]]), length(v_idx[[k]]))
  }
})

test_that("split_cv labels repeats and pads fold numbers", {
  res <- split_cv(list(iris), v = 10, repeats = 2, seed = 1)[[1]]
  expect_identical(names(res)[1:2], c("id", "id2"))
  expect_identical(unique(res$id), c("Repeat1", "Repeat2"))
  expect_identical(res$id2[1:2], c("Fold01", "Fold02"))
})

test_that("split_cv stratifies categorical and numeric variables", {
  res <- split_cv(list(iris), v = 5, strata = "Species", seed = 2)[[1]]
  counts <- vapply(res$validate, function(d) as.integer(table(d$Species)), integer(3))
  expect_true(all(counts == 10L))
  expect_silent(split_cv(list(mtcars), v = 4, strata = "mpg", breaks = 3))
})

test_that("split_cv seed is reproducible and does not disturb the RNG", {
  set.seed(9); ref <- runif(1)
  set.seed(9)
  a <- split_cv(list(iris), v = 3, seed = 1, materialize = FALSE)
  expect_identical(runif(1), ref)
  expect_identical(a, split_cv(list(iris), v = 3, seed = 1, materialize = FALSE))
})

test_that("split_cv out_type = 'df' returns plain data.frames with full factor levels", {
  res <- split_cv(list(iris), v = 3, seed = 1, out_type = "df")[[1]]
  expect_s3_class(res, "data.table")                       # fold table itself
  for (d in c(res$train, res$validate)) {
    expect_s3_class(d, "data.frame", exact = TRUE)
    expect_identical(levels(d$Species), levels(iris$Species))
  }
  ref <- iris[res$validate_idx[[1]], ]
  rownames(ref) <- NULL
  expect_equal(res$validate[[1]], ref)
  expect_error(split_cv(list(iris), v = 3, out_type = "tibble"), "out_type")
})

test_that("split_cv out_type does not change the folds", {
  a <- split_cv(list(iris), v = 3, seed = 5, out_type = "dt")[[1]]
  b <- split_cv(list(iris), v = 3, seed = 5, out_type = "df")[[1]]
  expect_identical(a$validate_idx, b$validate_idx)
  expect_equal(as.data.frame(a$train[[2]]), b$train[[2]])
})

test_that("split_cv validates its input", {
  expect_error(split_cv(iris), "wrap it in list")
  expect_error(split_cv(list()), "empty")
  expect_error(split_cv(list(iris[1:3, ]), v = 5), "fewer rows")
  expect_error(split_cv(list(iris), strata = "nope"), "absent")
  expect_error(split_cv(list(iris), v = 1), "`v`")
})
```

# Cross-validation inside a nested table: `nest_cv()`
    
```{r function-nest_cv}
#' Apply V-Fold Cross-Validation to Nested Data
#'
#' @description
#' `nest_cv` creates v-fold cross-validation splits for each nested data frame
#' of a nested `data.table` (e.g. the output of [w2l_nest()]) and returns one
#' row per fold, with the outer (non-nested) columns broadcast to every fold.
#' The cross-validation itself is performed by [split_cv()].
#'
#' @param data    A `data.frame` or `data.table` containing at least one nested
#'   `data.frame`/`data.table` column. A column named `data` is used if
#'   present, otherwise the first nested column.
#' @inheritParams split_cv
#'
#' @return A `data.table` with all non-nested columns of `data`, followed by
#'   the columns described in [split_cv()] (`id`, `id2`, `train_idx`,
#'   `validate_idx` and, if `materialize = TRUE`, `train` / `validate`, whose
#'   class follows `out_type`).
#'   Other nested columns are dropped (a message lists them). Non-nested
#'   columns must not use these names (an error is raised instead of
#'   creating duplicated columns).
#'
#' @seealso [split_cv()]
#'
#' @import data.table
#' @export
nest_cv <- function(data,
                    v           = 10L,
                    repeats     = 1L,
                    strata      = NULL,
                    breaks      = 4L,
                    pool        = 0.1,
                    seed        = NULL,
                    materialize = TRUE,
                    out_type    = "dt") {
  nest_dt <- data

  # -- 1. Input validation ----------------------------------------------------
  if (!is.data.frame(nest_dt))
    stop("`data` must be a data.frame or data.table. Received: ",
         paste(class(nest_dt), collapse = "/"), call. = FALSE)
  if (nrow(nest_dt) == 0L)
    stop("`data` must not be empty (0 rows).", call. = FALSE)

  # -- 2. Identify nested columns ----------------------------------------------
  nested_cols <- names(nest_dt)[vapply(nest_dt, function(col) {
    is.list(col) && length(col) > 0L &&
      all(vapply(col, is.data.frame, logical(1L)))
  }, logical(1L))]

  if (length(nested_cols) == 0L)
    stop("`data` contains no nested data.frame/data.table columns.\n",
         "  Column types detected: ",
         paste(names(nest_dt),
               vapply(nest_dt, function(x) class(x)[1L], character(1L)),
               sep = "=", collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)

  target_col <- if ("data" %in% nested_cols) "data" else nested_cols[1L]
  if (target_col != "data")
    message("[nest_cv] No nested column named 'data' found. Using '", target_col,
            "' instead.\n          Available nested columns: ",
            paste(nested_cols, collapse = ", "))
  if (length(nested_cols) > 1L)
    message("[nest_cv] Only '", target_col, "' is split; other nested column(s) ",
            "are dropped from the result: ",
            paste(setdiff(nested_cols, target_col), collapse = ", "))

  dt <- if (data.table::is.data.table(nest_dt)) nest_dt else data.table::as.data.table(nest_dt)
  non_nested_cols <- setdiff(names(dt), nested_cols)

  # -- 3. Delegate the CV work to split_cv() (single implementation) ----------
  cv_list <- split_cv(
    data        = dt[[target_col]],
    v           = v,
    repeats     = repeats,
    strata      = strata,
    breaks      = breaks,
    pool        = pool,
    seed        = seed,
    materialize = materialize,
    out_type    = out_type
  )

  # -- 4. Broadcast each row's metadata across its CV rows and bind ------------
  cv_dt <- data.table::rbindlist(cv_list, use.names = TRUE)
  if (length(non_nested_cols) == 0L) return(cv_dt)
  # Without this check cbind() would silently create duplicated column names
  # (e.g. a grouping column called `id`).
  .check_reserved(non_nested_cols, names(cv_dt), "nest_cv", "Grouping column(s)",
                  "these names are used for the cross-validation columns")

  n_cv <- vapply(cv_list, nrow, integer(1L))
  meta <- dt[rep(seq_len(nrow(dt)), n_cv), non_nested_cols, with = FALSE]
  cbind(meta, cv_dt)
}
```
  
```{r example-nest_cv}
# Example: Cross-validation for nested data.table demonstrations

# Setup test data
dt_nest <- w2l_nest(
  data = iris,                   # Input dataset
  cols = 1:2                     # Nest first 2 columns
)

# Example 1: Basic 2-fold cross-validation (reproducible)
nest_cv(
  data = dt_nest,                # Input nested data.table
  v = 2,                         # Number of folds (2-fold CV)
  seed = 123                     # Reproducible folds
)

# Example 2: Repeated 2-fold CV, keeping only the split objects
nest_cv(
  data = dt_nest,                # Input nested data.table
  v = 2,                         # Number of folds (2-fold CV)
  repeats = 2,                   # Number of repetitions
  seed = 123,
  materialize = FALSE            # No train/validate copies (saves memory)
)

# Example 3: data.frame subsets, ready for ASReml-R / lm() / glm()
cv_df <- nest_cv(dt_nest, v = 2, seed = 123, out_type = "df")
class(cv_df$train[[1]])        # "data.frame"

# Example 4: masking-style CV (keep all rows, hide validation phenotypes)
cv_idx <- nest_cv(dt_nest, v = 2, seed = 123, materialize = FALSE)
cv_idx[dt_nest, on = "name", full := i.data]   # attach the full nested table
masked <- as.data.frame(cv_idx$full[[1]])      # a copy: dt_nest stays intact
masked$value[cv_idx$validate_idx[[1]]] <- NA
sum(is.na(masked$value))       # validation records to be predicted
```

```{r tests-nest_cv}
test_that("nest_cv broadcasts metadata and partitions every nested table", {
  nd <- w2l_nest(iris, cols = 1:2, by = "Species")
  res <- nest_cv(nd, v = 5, seed = 1)
  expect_equal(nrow(res), 6L * 5L)
  expect_identical(names(res)[1:3], c("name", "Species", "id"))
  one <- res[name == "Sepal.Length" & Species == "setosa"]
  expect_identical(sort(unlist(one$validate_idx)), 1:50)
  expect_equal(nrow(one$train[[1]]) + nrow(one$validate[[1]]), 50L)
})

test_that("nest_cv is reproducible and supports materialize = FALSE", {
  nd <- w2l_nest(iris, cols = 1, by = "Species")
  a <- nest_cv(nd, v = 3, seed = 7, materialize = FALSE)
  b <- nest_cv(nd, v = 3, seed = 7, materialize = FALSE)
  expect_identical(a, b)
  expect_false(any(c("train", "validate") %in% names(a)))
})

test_that("nest_cv out_type = 'df' gives data.frame subsets", {
  nd <- w2l_nest(iris, cols = 1, by = "Species")
  res <- nest_cv(nd, v = 2, seed = 1, out_type = "df")
  expect_true(all(vapply(c(res$train, res$validate),
                         function(d) identical(class(d), "data.frame"), logical(1L))))
})

test_that("masking with validate_idx leaves the nested data untouched", {
  nd <- w2l_nest(iris, cols = 1:2, by = "Species")
  cv <- nest_cv(nd, v = 5, seed = 1, materialize = FALSE)
  cv[nd, on = c("name", "Species"), full := i.data]
  n_masked <- mapply(function(full, vidx) {
    d <- as.data.frame(full)
    d$value[vidx] <- NA
    sum(is.na(d$value))
  }, cv$full, cv$validate_idx)
  expect_identical(n_masked, lengths(cv$validate_idx))
  expect_false(anyNA(unlist(lapply(nd$data, `[[`, "value"))))
})

test_that("nest_cv validates its input", {
  expect_error(nest_cv(iris), "no nested")
})

test_that("nest_cv rejects grouping columns named like CV columns", {
  nd <- data.table::data.table(id = c("A", "B"),
                               data = list(data.frame(y = 1:20), data.frame(y = 1:20)))
  expect_error(nest_cv(nd, v = 5, seed = 1), "'id'")
})
```

# Shared folds for comparing models: `cv_folds()` and `apply_folds()`

When several models are compared (single- vs multi-trait, one group vs groups combined, ...), they should be validated on the same individuals. `cv_folds()` assigns every individual to a fold once, within each group and independently in each repeat; `apply_folds()` then cuts any nested table (from `w2l_nest()`, `c2p_nest()`, `r2p_nest()`, ...) into training / validation sets by matching the individual ID, optionally adding all records of the other groups to every training set.

```{r function-cv_folds}
#' Individual-level cross-validation folds shared across traits and models
#'
#' @description
#' `cv_folds()` assigns every **individual** (not every row) to one of `v`
#' folds, separately within each group (e.g. herd) and independently in each
#' repeat. The resulting fold table is meant to be created **once** and then
#' reused with [apply_folds()] for every trait, trait pair and model, so that
#' all compared models are validated on exactly the same individuals.
#'
#' Repeats are generated one after another (repeat 1 for all groups, then
#' repeat 2, ...), so with the same `seed` the first repeats do not change
#' when `repeats` is increased later.
#'
#' @param data A `data.frame` or `data.table` with one or more records per
#'   individual.
#' @param id Individual ID column (name or index). All records of an
#'   individual always fall into the same fold.
#' @param by Optional grouping column(s); folds are built within each group.
#'   An individual must belong to exactly one group.
#' @param v Number of folds (>= 2).
#' @param repeats Number of repeats (>= 1).
#' @param strata Optional column to stratify on (must be constant within an
#'   individual). Numeric columns are binned into `breaks` quantile bins and
#'   strata smaller than `pool` are merged, as in [split_cv()].
#' @param breaks,pool See [split_cv()].
#' @param seed Optional seed; the global random number stream is left untouched.
#'
#' @return A `data.table` with one row per individual and repeat: the `by`
#'   column(s), the `id` column, `rep` (`"Repeat01"`, ...) and `fold`
#'   (`"Fold1"`, ...): the fold in which the individual is validated.
#'
#' @seealso [apply_folds()], [cv_scenarios()]
#' @import data.table
#' @export
cv_folds <- function(data, id, by = NULL, v = 5L, repeats = 1L, strata = NULL,
                     breaks = 4L, pool = 0.1, seed = NULL) {
  if (!is.data.frame(data))
    stop("`data` must be a data.frame or data.table.", call. = FALSE)
  if (nrow(data) == 0L) stop("`data` must not be empty.", call. = FALSE)
  dt <- data.table::as.data.table(data)
  id_col <- .resolve_cols(id, names(dt), "id")
  if (length(id_col) != 1L) stop("`id` must be a single column.", call. = FALSE)
  by_cols <- setdiff(.resolve_cols(by, names(dt), "by", allow_null = TRUE), id_col)
  st_col  <- .resolve_cols(strata, names(dt), "strata", allow_null = TRUE)
  if (length(st_col) > 1L) stop("`strata` must be a single column.", call. = FALSE)
  v       <- .check_count(v, "v", min = 2L)
  repeats <- .check_count(repeats, "repeats", min = 1L)
  .check_reserved(c(id_col, by_cols), c("rep", "fold"), "cv_folds",
                  "`id` / `by` column(s)", "these names are used for the fold table")

  keys <- unique(dt[, unique(c(by_cols, id_col, st_col)), with = FALSE])
  if (anyNA(keys[[id_col]]))
    stop("[ cv_folds ] The `id` column contains NA.", call. = FALSE)
  if (anyDuplicated(keys[[id_col]])) {
    bad <- unique(keys[[id_col]][duplicated(keys[[id_col]])])
    stop("[ cv_folds ] Some individuals belong to more than one `by` group",
         if (length(st_col)) " or have more than one `strata` value", ": ",
         paste(utils::head(bad, 5L), collapse = ", "),
         if (length(bad) > 5L) sprintf(" ... (%d in total)", length(bad)),
         call. = FALSE)
  }

  grp <- if (length(by_cols)) {
    g <- keys[, by_cols, with = FALSE]
    data.table::set(g, j = ".g", value = 0L)
    g[, .g := .GRP, by = by_cols][[".g"]]
  } else rep(1L, nrow(keys))
  idx <- split(seq_len(nrow(keys)), grp)
  small <- vapply(idx, length, integer(1L)) < v
  if (any(small))
    stop(sprintf("[ cv_folds ] %d group(s) have fewer than v = %d individuals.",
                 sum(small), v), call. = FALSE)
  st_list <- if (length(st_col))
    lapply(idx, function(i) .make_strata(keys[[st_col]][i], breaks, pool))

  assign_all <- function() {
    f <- matrix(NA_integer_, nrow(keys), repeats)
    for (r in seq_len(repeats))
      for (g in seq_along(idx))
        f[idx[[g]], r] <- .assign_folds(length(idx[[g]]), v,
                                        if (length(st_col)) st_list[[g]])
    f
  }
  fmat <- .with_seed(seed, assign_all())

  fold_lab <- sprintf(paste0("Fold%0", nchar(v), "d"), seq_len(v))
  rep_lab  <- sprintf(paste0("Repeat%0", nchar(repeats), "d"), seq_len(repeats))
  base <- keys[, c(by_cols, id_col), with = FALSE]
  out <- data.table::rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(repeats), function(r) {
    b <- data.table::copy(base)
    data.table::set(b, j = "rep",  value = rep_lab[r])
    data.table::set(b, j = "fold", value = fold_lab[fmat[, r]])
    b
  }))
  data.table::setattr(out, "cv_id", id_col)
  data.table::setattr(out, "cv_by", by_cols)
  out[]
}
```

```{r example-cv_folds}
                  adg = rnorm(40), bf = rnorm(40))
folds <- cv_folds(dat, id = "id", by = "herd", v = 5, repeats = 2, seed = 1)
```

```{r tests-cv_folds}
make_dat <- function(n = 60, seed = 1) {
  set.seed(seed)
  data.frame(id = sprintf("i%03d", seq_len(n)),
             herd = rep(c("A", "B"), length.out = n),
             sex = sample(c("M", "F"), n, TRUE),
             adg = rnorm(n), bf = rnorm(n), fcr = rnorm(n),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

test_that("cv_folds partitions individuals within each group and repeat", {
  dat <- make_dat()
  f <- cv_folds(dat, id = "id", by = "herd", v = 5, repeats = 3, seed = 1)
  expect_equal(names(f), c("herd", "id", "rep", "fold"))
  expect_equal(nrow(f), 60 * 3)
  # every individual exactly once per repeat
  expect_true(all(f[, .N, by = .(id, rep)]$N == 1L))
  # balanced folds (6 per herd and fold)
  expect_true(all(f[, .N, by = .(herd, rep, fold)]$N == 6L))
  # repeats differ
  r1 <- f[rep == "Repeat1"][order(id)]$fold; r2 <- f[rep == "Repeat2"][order(id)]$fold
  expect_false(identical(r1, r2))
})

test_that("cv_folds is reproducible, leaves the global RNG alone, and extends repeats", {
  dat <- make_dat()
  set.seed(99); before <- runif(1); set.seed(99)
  a <- cv_folds(dat, "id", "herd", v = 5, repeats = 2, seed = 7)
  expect_equal(runif(1), before)
  b <- cv_folds(dat, "id", "herd", v = 5, repeats = 2, seed = 7)
  expect_equal(a, b)
  c10 <- cv_folds(dat, "id", "herd", v = 5, repeats = 3, seed = 7)
  expect_equal(c10[rep %in% c("Repeat1", "Repeat2")]$fold, a$fold)
})

test_that("cv_folds keeps repeated records of an individual together", {
  dat <- make_dat(20)
  dat2 <- rbind(dat, dat)                           # two records per individual
  f <- cv_folds(dat2, "id", "herd", v = 2, seed = 1)
  expect_equal(nrow(f), 20)
  cv <- apply_folds(w2l_nest(dat2, cols = "adg"), f)
  expect_true(all(vapply(cv$validate, function(d) all(table(d$id) == 2L), logical(1))))
})

test_that("cv_folds input checks", {
  dat <- make_dat(20)
  bad <- rbind(dat, transform(dat[1, ], herd = "B"))
  bad$herd[nrow(bad)] <- ifelse(dat$herd[1] == "A", "B", "A")
  expect_error(cv_folds(bad, "id", "herd", v = 2), "more than one")
  expect_error(cv_folds(dat, "id", "herd", v = 11), "fewer than")
  expect_error(cv_folds(dat, "id", v = 1), "v")
  names(dat)[2] <- "fold"
  expect_error(cv_folds(dat, "id", "fold"), "must not be named")
})

test_that("cv_folds stratifies", {
  dat <- make_dat(80)
  f <- cv_folds(dat, "id", "herd", v = 4, strata = "sex", seed = 3)
  tab <- merge(f, dat[, c("id", "sex")], by = "id")[, .N, by = .(herd, fold, sex)]
  rng <- tab[, diff(range(N)), by = .(herd, sex)]$V1
  expect_true(all(rng <= 1L))
})
```

```{r function-apply_folds}
#' Apply a shared fold table to any nested data
#'
#' @description
#' `apply_folds()` turns a nested table (from [w2l_nest()], [c2p_nest()],
#' [r2p_nest()] or built by hand) into training / validation sets using a
#' fold table from [cv_folds()]. Rows are matched to folds through the
#' individual ID, so single-trait, multi-trait and across-group models all
#' get identical validation individuals.
#'
#' Nested rows that differ only in the grouping column(s) of the fold table
#' (e.g. `w2l_nest(..., by = "herd")`) are merged first, and the grouping
#' column is put back inside the data (right after the ID column), so the
#' training set of every scenario carries the group as a possible fixed
#' effect.
#'
#' @param data A nested `data.table` / `data.frame` (a list-column named
#'   `data`, or the first data.frame list-column, is used), or a plain table.
#' @param folds A fold table from [cv_folds()].
#' @param ref `"none"`: train on the target group only. `"others"`: also add
#'   **all** records of the other groups to every training set (reference
#'   population enlarged by the other groups; they are never validated).
#' @param out_type `"dt"` (default) or `"df"` for the nested subsets.
#'
#' @return A `data.table` with the outer columns of `data`, the grouping
#'   column(s) of `folds` (the validated group), `rep`, `fold`, and the
#'   list-columns `train` and `validate`.
#'
#' @seealso [cv_folds()], [cv_scenarios()]
#' @import data.table
#' @export
apply_folds <- function(data, folds, ref = "none", out_type = "dt") {
  ref      <- .check_choice(ref, c("none", "others"), "ref")
  out_type <- .check_choice(out_type, c("dt", "df"), "out_type")
  if (!is.data.frame(data)) stop("`data` must be a data.frame or data.table.", call. = FALSE)
  if (!is.data.frame(folds) || !all(c("rep", "fold") %in% names(folds)))
    stop("`folds` must be a fold table created by cv_folds().", call. = FALSE)
  fk <- data.table::as.data.table(folds)
  key_cols <- setdiff(names(fk), c("rep", "fold"))
  id_col  <- attr(folds, "cv_id")
  by_cols <- attr(folds, "cv_by")
  if (is.null(id_col)) {                 # attributes lost: use the column layout
    id_col  <- key_cols[length(key_cols)]
    by_cols <- key_cols[-length(key_cols)]
  }
  if (ref == "others" && !length(by_cols))
    stop("`ref = \"others\"` needs a fold table built with `by`.", call. = FALSE)

  dt <- data.table::as.data.table(data)
  is_nested <- vapply(dt, function(x) is.list(x) && length(x) > 0L &&
                        all(vapply(x, is.data.frame, logical(1L))), logical(1L))
  if (!any(is_nested)) {
    dt <- data.table::data.table(data = list(dt))
    is_nested <- c(data = TRUE)
  }
  nested_cols <- names(dt)[is_nested]
  target <- if ("data" %in% nested_cols) "data" else nested_cols[1L]
  outer  <- names(dt)[!is_nested]
  .check_reserved(outer, c("rep", "fold", "train", "validate"), "apply_folds",
                  "Outer column(s)", "these names are used for the result")
  outer_by <- intersect(by_cols, outer)
  keep     <- setdiff(outer, outer_by)

  # -- group map: individual -> group (from the fold table) --------------------
  gmap <- unique(fk[, c(by_cols, id_col), with = FALSE])
  if (length(by_cols)) {
    glev <- unique(gmap[, by_cols, with = FALSE])
    gmap[glev[, .g := .I], on = by_cols, .g := i..g]
  } else {
    glev <- data.table::data.table(.g = 1L)
    gmap[, .g := 1L]
  }
  reps  <- unique(fk$rep)
  folds_lab <- sort(unique(fk$fold))
  fwide <- lapply(reps, function(r) fk[rep == r])

  # -- merge rows that differ only in the grouping column(s) -------------------
  units <- if (length(keep)) dt[, list(.rows = list(.I)), by = keep]
           else data.table::data.table(.rows = list(seq_len(nrow(dt))))
  take <- if (out_type == "df") function(d, i) data.table::setDF(d[i]) else function(d, i) d[i]

  res <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(units)), function(u) {
    rows <- units$.rows[[u]]
    d <- data.table::rbindlist(lapply(rows, function(i) {
      x <- data.table::copy(data.table::as.data.table(dt[[target]][[i]]))
      add <- setdiff(outer_by, names(x))
      if (length(add)) {
        for (b in add) data.table::set(x, j = b, value = dt[[b]][i])
        nm  <- setdiff(names(x), add)
        pos <- match(id_col, nm)
        if (!is.na(pos))
          data.table::setcolorder(x, c(nm[seq_len(pos)], add, nm[-seq_len(pos)]))
      }
      x
    }), use.names = TRUE, fill = TRUE)
    if (!id_col %in% names(d))
      stop(sprintf("[ apply_folds ] ID column '%s' not found in the nested data.", id_col),
           call. = FALSE)

    m  <- match(as.character(d[[id_col]]), as.character(gmap[[id_col]]))
    if (anyNA(m))
      warning(sprintf("[ apply_folds ] %d record(s) whose ID is not in `folds` were dropped.",
                      sum(is.na(m))), call. = FALSE)
    g_row <- gmap$.g[m]
    for (b in intersect(by_cols, names(d))) {     # group column inside the data
      bad <- !is.na(m) & as.character(d[[b]]) != as.character(gmap[[b]][m])
      if (any(bad, na.rm = TRUE))
        stop(sprintf("[ apply_folds ] Column '%s' in the data disagrees with `folds` for %d record(s).",
                     b, sum(bad, na.rm = TRUE)), call. = FALSE)
    }

    meta <- if (length(keep)) units[u, keep, with = FALSE] else NULL
    out <- list(); k <- 0L
    for (g in glev$.g) {
      in_g <- which(g_row == g)
      if (!length(in_g)) next
      other <- if (ref == "others") which(!is.na(g_row) & g_row != g) else integer(0)
      for (r in seq_along(reps)) {
        fr <- fwide[[r]]
        f_row <- fr$fold[match(as.character(d[[id_col]][in_g]), as.character(fr[[id_col]]))]
        for (f in folds_lab) {
          k <- k + 1L
          out[[k]] <- data.table::data.table(
            .g = g, rep = reps[r], fold = f,
            train    = list(take(d, c(in_g[f_row != f], other))),
            validate = list(take(d, in_g[f_row == f])))
        }
      }
    }
    out <- data.table::rbindlist(out)
    if (length(by_cols)) {
      out <- glev[out, on = ".g"]
      data.table::setcolorder(out, c(by_cols, "rep", "fold"))
    }
    out[, .g := NULL]
    if (!is.null(meta)) out <- cbind(meta[rep(1L, nrow(out))], out)
    out
  })
  data.table::rbindlist(res, use.names = TRUE)
}
```

```{r example-apply_folds}
dat <- data.frame(id = paste0("i", 1:40), herd = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 20),
                  adg = rnorm(40), bf = rnorm(40))
folds <- cv_folds(dat, id = "id", by = "herd", v = 5, seed = 1)
# single-trait, within herd
apply_folds(w2l_nest(dat, cols = c("adg", "bf"), by = "herd"), folds)
# single-trait, other herd added to the training set
apply_folds(w2l_nest(dat, cols = c("adg", "bf")), folds, ref = "others")
```

```{r tests-apply_folds}
  data.frame(id = sprintf("i%03d", seq_len(n)),
             herd = rep(c("A", "B"), length.out = n),

test_that("apply_folds gives identical validation individuals for any nesting", {
  dat <- make_dat()
  f <- cv_folds(dat, "id", "herd", v = 5, repeats = 2, seed = 1)
  ids <- function(cv) vapply(cv$validate, function(d) paste(sort(d$id), collapse = ","), "")
  key <- function(cv) paste(cv$herd, cv$rep, cv$fold)
  st  <- apply_folds(w2l_nest(dat, cols = c("adg", "bf"), by = "herd"), f)
  mt  <- apply_folds(c2p_nest(dat, cols = c("adg", "bf", "fcr")), f, ref = "others")
  ref <- tapply(ids(st), key(st), unique)
  expect_true(all(lengths(ref) == 1L))
  expect_equal(as.vector(unlist(ref[key(mt)])), ids(mt))
})

test_that("apply_folds: ref = 'none' vs 'others' and group column put back", {
  dat <- make_dat()
  f <- cv_folds(dat, "id", "herd", v = 5, seed = 1)
  a <- apply_folds(w2l_nest(dat, cols = "adg", by = "herd"), f, ref = "none")
  b <- apply_folds(w2l_nest(dat, cols = "adg", by = "herd"), f, ref = "others")
  expect_equal(nrow(a), 2 * 5)
  expect_equal(names(a$train[[1]])[1:2], c("id", "herd"))   # inserted after id
  expect_true(all(vapply(seq_len(nrow(a)), function(i)
    nrow(a$train[[i]]) + nrow(a$validate[[i]]) == 30, logical(1))))
  expect_true(all(vapply(seq_len(nrow(b)), function(i)
    nrow(b$train[[i]]) == nrow(a$train[[i]]) + 30, logical(1))))
  expect_true(all(vapply(seq_len(nrow(b)), function(i)
    all(b$validate[[i]]$herd == b$herd[i]), logical(1))))
  expect_true(all(vapply(seq_len(nrow(a)), function(i)
    !length(intersect(a$train[[i]]$id, a$validate[[i]]$id)), logical(1))))
})

test_that("apply_folds checks and warnings", {
  dat <- make_dat()
  f <- cv_folds(dat[dat$id != "i001", ], "id", "herd", v = 5, seed = 1)
  expect_warning(apply_folds(w2l_nest(dat, cols = "adg"), f), "not in `folds`")
  f0 <- cv_folds(dat, "id", v = 5, seed = 1)
  expect_error(apply_folds(w2l_nest(dat, cols = "adg"), f0, ref = "others"), "by")
  dat2 <- dat; dat2$herd[1] <- ifelse(dat$herd[1] == "A", "B", "A")
  f1 <- cv_folds(dat, "id", "herd", v = 5, seed = 1)
  expect_error(apply_folds(w2l_nest(dat2, cols = "adg"), f1), "disagrees")
  # works when the fold table lost its attributes
  f2 <- data.table::as.data.table(as.data.frame(f1))
  expect_equal(nrow(apply_folds(w2l_nest(dat, cols = "adg"), f2)), 10)
  expect_s3_class(apply_folds(w2l_nest(dat, cols = "adg"), f1, out_type = "df")$train[[1]],
                  "data.frame")
})
```

# Five genomic prediction scenarios in one call: `cv_scenarios()`

`cv_scenarios()` builds the parameter-estimation data and the cross-validation data of five usual scenarios (single- / two-trait, within one group / groups combined, and one trait treated as a different trait in each group) from one phenotype table and one fold table; `export_scenarios()` writes everything to disk, e.g. as input files for 'ASReml', 'DMU' or 'HIBLUP'.

```{r function-cv_scenarios}
#' Build parameter-estimation and cross-validation data for five GBLUP scenarios
#'
#' @description
#' One call builds, from a single phenotype table, the data for the usual
#' comparison of genomic prediction models across traits and groups (herds,
#' lines, ...), all validated on the **same individuals** via one fold table:
#'
#' | scenario | model | parameter data | training set |
#' |---|---|---|---|
#' | `st_sp` | single-trait, single group | trait x group | target group |
#' | `st_mp` | single-trait, groups combined | trait | target group + all other groups |
#' | `mt_sp` | two-trait, single group | trait pair x group | target group |
#' | `mt_mp` | two-trait, groups combined | trait pair | target group + all other groups |
#' | `mt_bt` | one trait treated as a different trait in each group | trait | target group + all other groups |
#'
#' Every data file keeps all non-trait columns (including `group`) in their
#' original order, and rows with missing phenotypes are kept, so the file
#' layout is identical across scenarios.
#'
#' @param data Phenotype table, one row per individual (or per record).
#' @param cols Trait columns (names or indices).
#' @param id Individual ID column.
#' @param group A single grouping column (e.g. `"test_herd"`).
#' @param folds Optional fold table from [cv_folds()]; created from `v`,
#'   `repeats`, `strata` and `seed` when `NULL`.
#' @inheritParams cv_folds
#' @param scenarios Scenarios to build (default: all five).
#' @param out_type `"dt"` or `"df"` for the nested subsets.
#'
#' @return A list of class `mintyr_scenarios`: `folds`, and for each scenario
#'   a list with `param` (nested data for parameter estimation) and `cv`
#'   (output of [apply_folds()]). Write it out with [export_scenarios()].
#'
#' @seealso [cv_folds()], [apply_folds()], [export_scenarios()]
#' @import data.table
#' @export
cv_scenarios <- function(data, cols, id, group, folds = NULL, v = 5L, repeats = 1L,
                         strata = NULL, seed = NULL,
                         scenarios = c("st_sp", "st_mp", "mt_sp", "mt_mp", "mt_bt"),
                         out_type = "dt") {
  if (!is.data.frame(data)) stop("`data` must be a data.frame or data.table.", call. = FALSE)
  dt <- data.table::as.data.table(data)
  cols   <- .resolve_cols(cols, names(dt), "cols")
  id_col <- .resolve_cols(id, names(dt), "id")
  grp    <- .resolve_cols(group, names(dt), "group")
  if (length(id_col) != 1L || length(grp) != 1L)
    stop("`id` and `group` must each be a single column.", call. = FALSE)
  if (any(c(id_col, grp) %in% cols))
    stop("`cols` must not contain the `id` or `group` column.", call. = FALSE)
  if (anyNA(dt[[grp]])) stop("The `group` column contains NA.", call. = FALSE)
  all_sc <- c("st_sp", "st_mp", "mt_sp", "mt_mp", "mt_bt")
  bad <- setdiff(scenarios, all_sc)
  if (length(bad) || !length(scenarios))
    stop("`scenarios` must be a subset of ", paste0("\"", all_sc, "\"", collapse = ", "),
         call. = FALSE)
  if (any(c("mt_sp", "mt_mp") %in% scenarios) && length(cols) < 2L)
    stop("Two-trait scenarios need at least two `cols`.", call. = FALSE)

  if (is.null(folds)) {
    folds <- cv_folds(dt, id = id_col, by = grp, v = v, repeats = repeats,
                      strata = strata, seed = seed)
  } else if (!identical(attr(folds, "cv_by") %||% setdiff(names(folds), c(id_col, "rep", "fold")), grp)) {
    stop("`folds` must be built with `by = \"", grp, "\"`.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  st  <- if (any(c("st_sp", "st_mp") %in% scenarios)) w2l_nest(dt, cols = cols)
  mt  <- if (any(c("mt_sp", "mt_mp") %in% scenarios)) c2p_nest(dt, cols = cols)
  out <- list(folds = folds)
  if ("st_sp" %in% scenarios)
    out$st_sp <- list(param = .split_nest(st, grp, out_type),
                      cv = apply_folds(st, folds, "none", out_type))
  if ("st_mp" %in% scenarios)
    out$st_mp <- list(param = .as_out(st, out_type),
                      cv = apply_folds(st, folds, "others", out_type))
  if ("mt_sp" %in% scenarios)
    out$mt_sp <- list(param = .split_nest(mt, grp, out_type),
                      cv = apply_folds(mt, folds, "none", out_type))
  if ("mt_mp" %in% scenarios)
    out$mt_mp <- list(param = .as_out(mt, out_type),
                      cv = apply_folds(mt, folds, "others", out_type))
  if ("mt_bt" %in% scenarios) {
    bt <- .bt_nest(dt, cols, grp)
    out$mt_bt <- list(param = .as_out(bt, out_type),
                      cv = apply_folds(bt, folds, "others", out_type))
  }
  structure(out, class = c("mintyr_scenarios", "list"))
}

#' @export
print.mintyr_scenarios <- function(x, ...) {
  f <- x$folds
  cat(sprintf("<mintyr_scenarios> %d individuals, %s x %s\n",
              data.table::uniqueN(f[[attr(f, "cv_id") %||% names(f)[length(names(f)) - 2L]]]),
              data.table::uniqueN(f$rep), data.table::uniqueN(f$fold)))
  for (s in setdiff(names(x), "folds"))
    cat(sprintf("  %-6s param: %3d data sets | cv: %4d train/validate pairs\n",
                s, nrow(x[[s]]$param), nrow(x[[s]]$cv)))
  invisible(x)
}

# -- internal helpers ----------------------------------------------------------

`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a)) b else a

#' Convert the nested subsets of a nested table to the requested class
#' @noRd
.as_out <- function(nested, out_type) {
  if (out_type == "df")
    nested[, data := lapply(data, function(d) data.table::setDF(data.table::copy(d)))]
  nested
}

#' Split every nested subset by `group`, keeping the group column inside
#' @noRd
.split_nest <- function(nested, group, out_type) {
  outer <- names(nested)[!vapply(nested, is.list, logical(1L))]
  res <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(nested)), function(i) {
    d  <- data.table::as.data.table(nested$data[[i]])
    lv <- unique(d[[group]])
    o  <- nested[rep(i, length(lv)), outer, with = FALSE]
    data.table::set(o, j = group, value = lv)
    data.table::set(o, j = "data", value = lapply(lv, function(l) d[d[[group]] == l]))
    o
  })
  .as_out(data.table::rbindlist(res), out_type)
}

#' One trait as a different trait per group: all non-trait columns are kept
#' and the trait is spread into one column per group level.
#' @noRd
.bt_nest <- function(dt, cols, group) {
  lv <- as.character(unique(dt[[group]]))
  covs <- setdiff(names(dt), cols)
  clash <- intersect(lv, covs)
  if (length(clash))
    stop("Group level(s) clash with existing column names: ",
         paste(clash, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  g <- as.character(dt[[group]])
  data.table::data.table(
    name = cols,
    data = lapply(cols, function(tr) {
      d <- dt[, covs, with = FALSE]
      for (l in lv) {
        x <- dt[[tr]]
        x[g != l] <- NA
        data.table::set(d, j = l, value = x)
      }
      d
    }))
}
utils::globalVariables(c(".g", "i..g", "data"))
```

```{r example-cv_scenarios}
                  sex = sample(c("M", "F"), 60, TRUE),

sc
sc$mt_bt$cv$train[[1]]
```

```{r tests-cv_scenarios}
make_dat <- function(n = 60, seed = 1) {
  set.seed(seed)
  data.frame(id = sprintf("i%03d", seq_len(n)),
             herd = rep(c("A", "B"), length.out = n),
             sex = sample(c("M", "F"), n, TRUE),
             adg = rnorm(n), bf = rnorm(n), fcr = rnorm(n),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

test_that("cv_scenarios builds five scenarios with a common layout", {
  dat <- make_dat()
  dat$adg[1:5] <- NA
  sc <- cv_scenarios(dat, cols = c("adg", "bf", "fcr"), id = "id", group = "herd",
                     v = 5, repeats = 2, seed = 1)
  expect_s3_class(sc, "mintyr_scenarios")
  expect_equal(names(sc), c("folds", "st_sp", "st_mp", "mt_sp", "mt_mp", "mt_bt"))
  expect_equal(vapply(sc[-1], function(s) nrow(s$cv), 1), rep(c(3, 3, 3, 3, 3) * 2 * 5 * 2, 1),
               ignore_attr = TRUE)
  expect_equal(nrow(sc$st_sp$param), 6); expect_equal(nrow(sc$mt_mp$param), 3)
  # NA rows kept
  expect_equal(nrow(sc$st_mp$param$data[[1]]), 60)
  # mt_bt: one column per herd, covariates kept, same columns in train/validate
  bt <- sc$mt_bt$cv
  expect_true(all(c("sex", "herd", "A", "B") %in% names(bt$train[[1]])))
  expect_identical(names(bt$train[[1]]), names(bt$validate[[1]]))
  v1 <- bt$validate[[1]]; expect_true(all(is.na(v1[[setdiff(c("A", "B"), bt$herd[1])]])))
  # same columns in parameter and CV files of the single-group scenario
  expect_identical(names(sc$st_sp$param$data[[1]]), names(sc$st_sp$cv$train[[1]]))
  expect_output(print(sc), "mintyr_scenarios")
  expect_error(cv_scenarios(dat, cols = "adg", id = "id", group = "herd", scenarios = "mt_sp"),
               "at least two")
})
```

```{r function-export_scenarios}
#' Write the output of cv_scenarios() to disk
#'
#' Writes `<path>/<dir>/param_est_data/...` and `<path>/<dir>/cv_data/...`
#' for every scenario with [export_nest()], e.g.
#' `cv_data/adg/nls/Repeat01/Fold1/train.txt`.
#'
#' @param x Output of [cv_scenarios()].
#' @param path Root folder.
#' @param dirs Optional named character vector of folder names per scenario,
#'   e.g. `c(st_sp = "2.1.st_sp")`; scenario names are used otherwise.
#' @param na Missing-value code written to the files (default `"."`).
#' @inheritParams export_nest
#' @return The written file paths, invisibly.
#' @export
export_scenarios <- function(x, path = tempdir(), dirs = NULL, na = ".",
                             file_type = "txt", quote = FALSE, ...) {
  if (!inherits(x, "mintyr_scenarios"))
    stop("`x` must be the output of cv_scenarios().", call. = FALSE)
  grp <- attr(x$folds, "cv_by")
  files <- character(0)
  for (s in setdiff(names(x), "folds")) {
    d <- if (!is.null(dirs) && !is.na(dirs[s])) dirs[[s]] else s
    p <- x[[s]]$param
    pby <- names(p)[!vapply(p, is.list, logical(1L))]
    files <- c(files, suppressMessages(export_nest(
      p, by = pby, cols = "data", path = file.path(path, d, "param_est_data"),
      file_type = file_type, na = na, quote = quote, ...)))
    cv <- x[[s]]$cv
    cby <- names(cv)[!vapply(cv, is.list, logical(1L))]
    files <- c(files, suppressMessages(export_nest(
      cv, by = cby, cols = c("train", "validate"), path = file.path(path, d, "cv_data"),
      file_type = file_type, na = na, quote = quote, ...)))
  }
  invisible(files)
}
```

```{r example-export_scenarios}
dat <- data.frame(id = paste0("i", 1:40), herd = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 20),
                  adg = rnorm(40), bf = rnorm(40))
sc <- cv_scenarios(dat, cols = c("adg", "bf"), id = "id", group = "herd",
                   v = 2, seed = 1, scenarios = c("st_sp", "mt_bt"))
files <- export_scenarios(sc, path = file.path(tempdir(), "gblup"))
head(files)
```

```{r tests-export_scenarios}
make_dat <- function(n = 60, seed = 1) {
  set.seed(seed)
  data.frame(id = sprintf("i%03d", seq_len(n)),
             herd = rep(c("A", "B"), length.out = n),
             sex = sample(c("M", "F"), n, TRUE),
             adg = rnorm(n), bf = rnorm(n), fcr = rnorm(n),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

test_that("export_scenarios writes all files with the missing-value code", {
  dat <- make_dat(20); dat$adg[1] <- NA
  sc <- cv_scenarios(dat, cols = c("adg", "bf"), id = "id", group = "herd",
                     v = 2, seed = 1, scenarios = c("st_sp", "mt_bt"))
  p <- file.path(tempdir(), "sc_test"); unlink(p, recursive = TRUE)
  files <- export_scenarios(sc, path = p, dirs = c(st_sp = "2.1.st_sp"))
  expect_true(all(file.exists(files)))
  expect_true(dir.exists(file.path(p, "2.1.st_sp", "cv_data")))
  expect_true(dir.exists(file.path(p, "mt_bt", "param_est_data")))
  expect_equal(sum(grepl("cv_data", files)), 2 * (2 * 2 * 2 * 2))  # 2 scenarios x 2 traits x 2 herds x 2 folds x {train, validate}
  txt <- readLines(file.path(p, "2.1.st_sp", "param_est_data", "adg",
                             dat$herd[1], "data.txt"))
  expect_true(any(grepl("\t\\.$", txt)))
  expect_false(any(grepl("\tNA", txt)))
})
```
